intro: A graph-level prediction needs one representation per graph even when graphs contain different numbers of nodes. Pooling combines node features while discarding their arbitrary order.
task: Group node rows by graph ID and produce sum, mean or coordinate-wise maximum readouts. Explore how each choice responds when the same nodes are duplicated.
requirements: features is a nonempty (N,D) matrix. batch is an integer vector of length N, excluding booleans, whose distinct IDs are exactly 0 through G-1 with no missing graph.
mode is 'sum', 'mean' or 'max'. Return a (G,D) NumPy array with one row per graph ID, even when node rows are interleaved.

Sum and mean reduce whole node rows; max is computed separately for each feature and must handle all-negative features. Reject empty input or gaps in graph IDs rather than inventing values for empty graphs.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Use graph IDs, not row blocks
hints.body: Nodes belonging to one graph need not be adjacent in the input.

hints.title: Think about duplication
hints.body: Duplicating every node changes sum pooling but leaves mean and maximum unchanged.

explanation: Readout is invariant to node order within each graph. The three modes preserve different information: sums carry size, means average it away, and maxima emphasize the strongest value of each feature.
A maximum vector need not equal any particular node’s feature vector because different coordinates may come from different nodes.
Ported the upstream sum, mean and max readouts to NumPy. Added contiguous-ID validation so empty groups cannot silently create NaN or negative-infinity outputs.
